# PHP Runner (`eyevinn-php-runner`)

php-runner is a container runtime for deploying PHP applications on Eyevinn Open Source Cloud as “My Apps”. It clones your Git repository (public or private), optionally targets a branch and subdirectory for monorepos, installs dependencies with Composer when a composer.json is present, and serves your app on Apache with mod_php (PHP 8.3). It also auto-detects common PHP framework docroots (like public/index.php) or lets you pin the entry directory explicitly, with .htaccess and mod_rewrite enabled so typical framework routing works out of the box.

As a managed OSC service, php-runner removes the work of packaging and operating your own runtime: you provide the repo URL and it provisions, builds, and starts the app for you, including a build-time loading server that reports health while dependencies are installing and signals failures if the build breaks. When you need extra setup beyond Composer, you can include a setup.sh that runs before Apache starts, without maintaining a custom base image.

php-runner also plugs into OSC-native capabilities: token-based authentication, build status signaling, and optional config service support to load runtime environment variables at startup (including secrets managed through OSC), so you can keep configuration out of container env vars and wire it into the rest of your OSC workflow.

[Source](https://github.com/Eyevinn/php-runner)

## Example

```terraform
resource "osc_instance" "example" {
  service_id = "eyevinn-php-runner"
  name       = "myrunner"

  parameters = {
    SourceUrl        = "..."
    # ConfigService    = "..."
    # SubPath          = "..."
    # AnalyticsService = "..."
    # OscEntry         = "..."
  }

  sensitive_parameters = {
    GitHubToken = var.git_hub_token
    OscAccessToken = var.osc_access_token
    ConfigApiKey = var.config_api_key
  }
}
```

Commented lines are optional parameters. Values marked `"..."` need a real value. Outputs are `url`, `external_ip`, `external_port` and the raw `instance` document, see the `osc_instance` resource.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SourceUrl` | string | yes | HTTPS URL of the Git repository to clone and serve, for example https://github.com/your-org/your-php-app. Append #branchname to use a specific branch; otherwise the default branch is used. |
| `GitHubToken` | string | no | Personal access token (for example a GitHub PAT) used to clone a private repository. Leave empty for public repositories. Sensitive, set it in `sensitive_parameters`. |
| `OscAccessToken` | string | no | OSC runner token used to authenticate with the OSC config service when loading environment variables at startup. Only used together with ConfigService; leave empty if you do not use the config service. Sensitive, set it in `sensitive_parameters`. |
| `ConfigService` | string | no | Name of the OSC config service to load environment variables from at startup. Only used together with OscAccessToken; the variables are loaded before dependencies are installed, and a failure to load is logged without stopping the build. |
| `ConfigApiKey` | string | no | API key for authentication Sensitive, set it in `sensitive_parameters`. |
| `SubPath` | string | no | Subdirectory inside the cloned repository to use as the app root, for monorepos, for example services/my-php-app. Leave empty to use the repository root. |
| `AnalyticsService` | string | no | Configuration option for analyticsservice |
| `OscEntry` | string | no | Overrides the auto-detected document root: a directory relative to the app root, for example public. Without it the runner looks for index.php in public/, then web/, then the app root. |

The instance `name` must match `^\w+$` and be unique per service within the workspace. OSC lowercases it and allows at most 20 characters.

Parameter values are strings; booleans take `"true"` or `"false"`. Reference an `osc_secret` as `osc_secret.<name>.ref` to keep a value out of the instance configuration. This page is generated from the OSC catalog; the provider validates against the live catalog when planning.
